requirement: Phase 1–6 modules, routes and tests are kept; the corrective work extends them and removes nothing
note: The whole Phase 1–6 suite is re-run (TESTING.md). No migration, no removed route, no removed test; two Phase 6 tests were not weakened (the browser script s10 changed one expected sentence because the plan wording was intentionally improved).

requirement: A stock SearXNG answers 403 to every JSON request and its bot limiter answers 429; PredictAI reported both as 'blocked'. A ready-made local configuration is shipped and the message names the exact fix
note: Verified against the SearXNG behaviour its documentation describes, using a local stand-in. A real SearXNG container was not run here.

source: §2 Request construction, parsing, URL validation, duplicates, metadata, dates
requirement: JSON request carries only the query; results are parsed with title, URL, text, engines, score and date; unsafe or malformed URLs and duplicates are dropped
'Search tools → Test now' checks each provider and says what works, what fails and how to fix it; it contacts only providers that are switched on

source: §2 Actual root cause of irrelevant results
requirement: A question is reduced to topic phrases and every provider gets queries in its own syntax, precise to broad (Phase 6 sent one pile of loose keywords plus filler words to all of them)

source: §2 Timeouts, retry, rate limits, unavailable providers
requirement: Each failure is named in plain words, retried only where that is safe, and listed on the result; arXiv requests are serialised and spaced across the whole process
note: The gate is per process: run research on one server process when using arXiv.

source: §2 Ranking, duplicate removal, retrieval timestamps, dates
requirement: Results are ranked fairly across providers, duplicates by canonical address and title are removed, irrelevant pages are dropped and counted, and every source keeps its retrieval time

source: §2 Meaningful error and fallback; never fabricated results
requirement: When a provider is down the others still answer, the failure is shown with its reason, and with nothing found the answer says so and holds no invented conclusion
Official MediaWiki API: search by keywords, summary, categories, page address, revision and last-modified time; spelling suggestion only when nothing matched
note: Tested against recorded response shapes, not live Wikipedia.

source: Addendum §1 Wikipedia: full relevant sections, tables, lists, references
requirement: The article is read as sections with headings, paragraphs, lists, tables (one sentence per row), equations and references; long articles are read by the sections that match the question

source: Addendum §1 Wikipedia: redirects, disambiguation, missing pages, duplicates
requirement: Handled and reported, never silently followed

source: Addendum §1 Wikipedia: API failures, rate limits, malformed answers, timeouts
requirement: Named errors; rate limits retried then reported; the refusal message names the contact setting

source: Addendum §1 Wikipedia: attribution and tertiary source
requirement: Every Wikipedia item carries its permanent link, licence and the label 'encyclopedia (tertiary source)'

source: Addendum §2 arXiv: search by title, author, abstract, keyword, category, identifier; metadata
requirement: Documented field queries, syntax checked before sending; identifier or URL looked up directly; authors, dates, categories, DOI, links returned
note: Tested against recorded Atom responses, not live arXiv.

source: Addendum §2 arXiv: full text and structure
requirement: Full text from arXiv's HTML version, else the PDF; sections, equations, tables kept; scanned, heading-less or stub pages handled and reported
note: PDFs have no maths markup (equations are the text layer's approximation, labelled so) and multi-column layouts can interleave lines. Verified on small generated PDFs, not on real papers.

requirement: The latest version is marked and dated, the full submission history can be read, an older version is read when asked and labelled as not the latest

source: Addendum §2 arXiv: preprint label; abstract is not the paper
requirement: Every item is labelled a preprint; a result states whether it holds the full text or only the abstract; the abstract comes from the API and is labelled

source: Addendum §2 arXiv: usage limits, caching, retry, timeouts
requirement: One request at a time, 3 s apart (15 s for the website pages), a cool-down after a refusal, robots.txt honoured for paper files, only extracted text cached
note: Single-process only; arXiv's terms count requests across all of a client's machines.

requirement: Question understanding, objective, parts, per-part sources and queries; simple, detailed, comparative, technical, academic and multi-step plans; follow-up questions; history
'In short' (one line per part, labelled by evidence kind), part-by-part blocks, what was calculated, outside sources by kind, comparison, uncertainties
note: Answers are quotations and fixed-template sentences chosen by ranked matching; no language model writes them. They are accurate but plain.

requirement: Disagreeing numbers and statements are shown side by side; single sources, preprints, an encyclopedia, samples and unread pages are listed as uncertainty
note: Conflict detection is by wording and numbers; subtle conflicts can be missed and the result says so.

source: §3 Citations on every supported claim, checked
requirement: A conclusion is a quotation (or a calculated sentence) with its source; each citation is re-checked against the saved source or rebuilt from the stored calculation

source: Addendum §3 Follow-ups on retrieved articles and papers
requirement: A follow-up reuses the saved copy of the earlier article or paper (the sections that were read), so it needs no new request; with web on it plans its own phrases for approval
note: With web off a follow-up can only use the sections the earlier question read.

source: §4 First-class dataset research through existing authorisation and the Phase 4/5 services
requirement: A selected dataset is opened only through the owner's own access check; schema, profile, quality, relationships, group comparisons, statistics, models, importance and evaluation come from the Phase 4/5 services
note: A column is recognised in a question by its full name (a question saying 'seats' does not match 'seats_available').

source: §4 No invented numbers; Python calculates, text only interprets
requirement: Every sentence is a fixed template over a stored result; the citation records the run and the check rebuilds the sentence from it, so an edited result or sentence fails
Only aggregates reach the answer (no rows, no free text); a dataset too large for one run is sampled and the sample is stated
Two datasets are described and compared with their real sizes and means; a single dataset says it cannot be compared

source: §4 Numeric, categorical, mixed, missing and suspicious values
requirement: Statistics match independent calculations (pandas, correlation ratio); identifier columns are never reported as relationships
The dataset is analysed first; topic phrases only go to the approved providers; outside passages are listed beside, never merged with, the calculated findings

source: §5 Calculated findings kept apart from external claims; no causation
requirement: An outside source never changes a calculated number; the comparison is by shared words and says so; an association is never called a cause
note: The comparison is word-match only: it cannot tell whether an outside passage agrees or disagrees in meaning.

source: §6 Documents, datasets, earlier analyses, models, web and bundles together, with provenance
requirement: Each statement carries its kind (your document, calculation, model estimate, Wikipedia, preprint, web page); earlier research bundles can be read by later research
note: An 'AI interpretation' label is used only when the person asks for AI wording; the default path uses no model.

requirement: Relevance, evidence coverage, numerical accuracy, calculated-versus-external separation and source quality were added to the Phase 6 checks (citation correctness, freshness, contradictions, unsupported claims, uncertainty, completeness)
With nothing found the answer says so and holds no conclusions

source: §8 Question input, project, dataset and document selection, web toggle, progress, plan visibility
requirement: The New research page offers datasets and documents of the project, the providers that are available and allowed (all selected by default), and shows exactly which phrases each provider would be sent
implementation: frontend pages/research/NewResearchPage.jsx, frontend pages/research/SessionPage.jsx, frontend features/research/plan.js
note: Also exercised in the browser run scripts/e2e/s11.mjs (11/11) on a stand-in backend.

source: §8 Combined report, dataset findings, statistical summaries, evidence and citation inspection
requirement: A report card (answer, parts, calculated results, outside sources, side-by-side comparison, uncertainty); a citation opens the calculation or the original page
implementation: frontend pages/research/ReportCard.jsx, frontend pages/research/BundlePage.jsx, frontend pages/research/CitationDialog.jsx, frontend features/research/report.js
note: Browser run s11 on a stand-in backend.

source: §8 Follow-up questions and history; Addendum §3 search Wikipedia and arXiv independently
requirement: A follow-up form on every result; a 'Search tools' tab to test each provider, search one provider and open an article or paper section by section
implementation: frontend pages/research/FollowUpForm.jsx, frontend pages/research/SearchToolsPanel.jsx, frontend pages/research/ProjectResearchPage.jsx, frontend features/research/searchtools.js
note: Browser run s11 on a stand-in backend.

requirement: `npm run build` (Vite) succeeds
note: Vite could not be installed in the build environment (no network). The app was bundled with esbuild as a stand-in; that is not the production build.

requirement: Datasets, sessions, bundles and the direct provider endpoints answer only for the owner of the project; others get the same 'not found'
The direct search/open endpoints refuse private-looking phrases and file/credential/private-address URLs before anything is sent; the fetcher re-checks every redirect
Text in an article, paper or page is quoted, never obeyed; instruction-like text is removed or the source held back

source: §9 Private data and consent; document and dataset privacy
requirement: Web research needs the server, person and project switches and the approved phrases; no row, cell, free text or file name is ever put in a phrase; a dataset-only question sends nothing
Contract examples and bundles carry no key, e-mail address or planted private value
New automated tests for web search, query construction, research reports, datasets, combined research, Wikipedia, arXiv, HTTP endpoints, contracts and the frontend; none needs an external service
note: Counts and results are in TESTING.md; live-service tests were not run.

source: §11 Complete source, dependencies, config templates, migrations, tests, setup instructions, mapping, report
requirement: The release archive holds every file the tests read and nothing local (no .env, keys, databases, environments or caches)
note: No migration was needed: the corrective work adds no table or column.

requirement: The documents say the platform is not production-ready and that the quality assessment is scheduled after Phase 12
Louis XVI = Louis 16 = Louis the Sixteenth; XVIII, XVII and XIV are other people; sources are ranked by identity, not word overlap
note: Fixed rule set for regnal names and demonyms; other kinds of ambiguity are only caught where a rule exists.

requirement: A task-aware outline per kind of question (overview, causes, comparison, methodology...); an optional local-AI interpretation can only add validated parts that the person approves, never queries
note: The AI interpretation was tested with a stand-in model only.

requirement: Off-subject, wrong-person, wrong-kind and out-of-context results are set aside with a stated reason; with nothing appropriate the answer says so
note: Tuned on the modelled corpus in tests/history_corpus.py; real pages will differ.

requirement: Exact title and alias lookup, section-level reading, section citations
note: Against a modelled MediaWiki, not the live service.

requirement: Used only when the subject fits or the person asks (auto / always / never); no-relevant-results is told apart from a failed provider; preprint warnings are kept
note: Against a modelled arXiv, not the live service.

requirement: Connectivity is verified; an unreachable or failing instance is shown as unavailable, never as success
note: Real TCP to a local stand-in; no real SearXNG was reachable (see scripts/live_research_check.py).

requirement: Whole sentences; running headers, footers and page numbers removed; page citations; document text never sent outside
note: Checked on a generated stand-in PDF, not the real french rev.pdf. A PDF uploaded earlier keeps its old text until it is uploaded again.

requirement: An explanation built only from checked relevant evidence, with the unknowns stated; statements stay quotations
note: Fixed-template wording over extracted sentences; an optional AI wording step was not changed.

requirement: Louis XVI; causes of the Revolution; two kings; economic condition; methodology of an ML paper; SearXNG down
note: Run against modelled providers and a stand-in PDF.

requirement: A clarification prompt, arXiv mode, AI-planning switch, skipped providers, provider statuses, rejected results and the explanation are shown
